name: MonarchToggleBlock
title: ToggleBlock
summary: A collapsible section of a document: a summary line that shows or hides the content indented under it.
whenToUse: In a document or an article, for details most readers can skip: a long explanation, an appendix, the answer to a question.
whenNotToUse: For a section of a settings screen or a form use MonarchCollapsible. For several sections where one opens at a time use an accordion.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchToggleBlock(summary: String, expanded: Boolean, onExpandedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, expandedLabel: String? = null, collapsedLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable public fun MonarchToggleBlock(summary: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, initiallyExpanded: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, expandedLabel: String? = null, collapsedLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

options.name: summary
options.description: The line that stays visible; it is the name of the button.

options.name: expanded
options.description: First overload: whether the content is shown, kept by the app, for example to save it with the document.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: First overload: called with the new state when the user activates the summary or uses the TalkBack expand or collapse action.

options.name: initiallyExpanded
options.description: Second overload: whether the content shows at first. The block then keeps its own state with rememberSaveable.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can activate the summary.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: A chevron that points down, after the summary; it turns half a turn while expanded. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: expandedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Expanded" state of MonarchCollapsible.

options.name: collapsedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Collapsed" state of MonarchCollapsible.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions of the summary.

options.name: content
options.description: The content that is shown and hidden.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Only the summary; the content is not composed.

states.name: expanded
states.description: The content shows under the summary, indented 24dp from the start edge; the chevron points up.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The summary and chevron take the disabled text color and the summary does not respond.

appearance: The summary uses the label type in the default text color and the chevron the muted text color, as MonarchCollapsible; there is no surface, so the block sits on the document background in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ToggleBlock is also a Tiptap editor node with an editable summary and keyboard shortcuts; Android has no Monarch rich-text editor, so only the read view is offered, as on iOS. The web names its button "Show section" or "Hide section" and draws a leading chevron; on Android the summary is the name of the button and the state is spoken as "Expanded" or "Collapsed", and the chevron comes after the summary, because the block is MonarchCollapsible, whose icon slot is trailing. Monarch bundles no icons, so the chevron is optional. The uncontrolled overload replaces the web's defaultOpen.
accessibility: The summary line is one button named by the summary, with the state "Expanded" or "Collapsed" and the TalkBack expand and collapse actions.
Hidden content leaves the composition, so TalkBack does not reach it.
The summary line is at least 48dp high and the whole line responds to touch.
The content appears at once when the user has turned animations off.
edgeCases: A long summary wraps; nothing is cut at font scale 2.0.
State inside the content is lost when it is hidden; hoist it if it must survive closing.
The indent is measured from the start edge, so it is on the right in right-to-left layouts.
